items.subtitle: 故事
items.summary: Chang’e takes both magic pills and discovers the cost of an impulsive choice.
items.learningFocus: Notice 月 (moon); discuss choices and taking responsibility.
items.transcript:
故事梗概（非逐字字幕）

后羿从西王母那里得到两颗不死药：吃一颗可以长生，吃两颗还能升天。嫦娥在两人留在人间与自己回到天上之间犹豫。趁后羿外出，她独自服下两颗药，身体随即飞向天空。到了寒冷的月宫，她才发现那里十分寂寞，只有桂树旁的小兔不停捣药。嫦娥后悔了，却无法再回到丈夫身边。这个版本提醒我们，作出选择前要考虑后果，并为自己的行为负责。
items.transcriptEn:
Story summary (not word-for-word subtitles)

Hou Yi receives two magic pills from the Queen Mother of the West. One pill lets a person live forever; two pills let them fly to heaven. Chang’e cannot decide whether to stay on Earth with her husband or return to heaven. While Hou Yi is away, she takes both pills and floats up into the sky. In the cold palace on the moon, she finds herself alone, with only a little rabbit making medicine by a tree. She feels sorry but cannot return to her husband. This version invites us to think about the results of our choices and take responsibility for what we do.

items.subtitle: 故事
items.summary: A farmer waits for the same lucky accident to happen again.
items.learningFocus: Listen for 兔 (rabbit); discuss why waiting cannot replace effort.
items.transcript:
故事梗概（非逐字字幕）

一只奔跑的兔子撞上树根死去，碰巧被田间的农夫捡到。农夫把这次意外收获当作省力的好办法，从此不再认真耕种，每天守在树旁等下一只兔子。日子过去，田里的杂草已经超过庄稼，他却再也没有得到兔子，反而成了人们的笑谈。这个寓言提醒我们，不能把偶然的好运当作必然的结果，更不能拿侥幸代替劳动。
items.transcriptEn:
Story summary (not word-for-word subtitles)

A running rabbit bumps into a tree stump and dies. A farmer happens to find it in his field. He thinks this lucky surprise is an easy way to get food. He stops caring for his crops and waits by the tree for another rabbit. Days pass. Weeds grow taller than his crops, but no more rabbits come. People laugh at his mistake. The story reminds us not to expect the same lucky accident to happen again, and not to let wishful thinking replace hard work.

items.subtitle: 故事
items.summary: A steady tortoise races a very confident rabbit.
items.learningFocus: Compare 快 (fast) and 慢 (slow); talk about keeping going.
items.transcript:
故事梗概（非逐字字幕）

乌龟和兔子约定比赛跑步，以一棵大树为终点。兔子很快跑到前面，觉得乌龟不可能追上自己，就在途中睡起觉来。乌龟虽然爬得慢，却一直没有停下。兔子醒来后急忙追赶，还是没能赶上已经到达大树的乌龟，惭愧地低下了头。故事最后请小朋友思考：速度快为什么不一定能赢，始终坚持为什么重要？
items.transcriptEn:
Story summary (not word-for-word subtitles)

A tortoise and a hare agree to race to a big tree. The hare runs far ahead. He is so sure the tortoise cannot catch up that he stops for a nap. The tortoise moves slowly but keeps going. When the hare wakes up, he hurries after the tortoise, but it is too late. The tortoise has already reached the tree. The hare feels ashamed. Think together: why does being fast not always mean winning, and why does keeping going matter?

items.subtitle: 故事
items.summary: A drawing contest changes when someone adds too much.
items.learningFocus: Notice 蛇 (snake) and 足 (foot); discuss when to stop adding things.
items.transcript:
故事梗概（非逐字字幕）

几个人用一壶酒作彩头，比谁先画好一条蛇。一人首先完成，却又得意地给蛇添起脚来。就在他继续添画时，另一人画好了没有脚的蛇，拿走了酒壶，并指出加脚之后的形象已经不像蛇，倒像蜥蜴。先画好的人因为多做了无用的部分，失去了原本可以得到的奖励。这个故事提醒我们，完成目标之后，也要分清什么是必要的，什么是多余的。
items.transcriptEn:
Story summary (not word-for-word subtitles)

Some people hold a drawing contest, with a jug of wine as the prize. The first person to finish a snake feels proud and starts adding feet. While he is still drawing, someone else finishes a snake without feet and takes the prize. A snake with feet no longer looks like a snake; it looks like a lizard. By adding something that was not needed, the first person loses the reward he could have won. The story asks us to notice when a job is finished and when adding more does not help.
